plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $26. This means bidding exactly $26 eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I only win if the prize is genuinely worth more than the second-highest bid. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-round game, strategic complexity is reduced. Bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value. Since my value is $18, and values are independently drawn, there's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value. Bidding $18 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more than my bid, which perfectly aligns my incentives. The second-price auction mechanism makes truth-telling the optimal long-term strategy.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly one's private value ($21) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. This eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I won't pay more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, strategic complexity is reduced. I'll bid my true value to maximize potential profit.
